title: Gauge freedom and efficient algorithms for Lindbladian learning
authors: Steven T Flammia, Savar D Sinha, Yu Tong
abstract: We study the problem of learning a local Lindbladian in the presence of state-preparation-and-measurement (SPAM) noise. Although recent work has developed scalable learning algorithms under idealized access assumptions, SPAM can make distinct Lindbladians experimentally indistinguishable, thus making part of the Lindbladian fundamentally unlearnable. We give a sharp characterization of this obstruction for bounded-degree local Lindbladians. We identify a family of locality-preserving gauge transformations that commutes with trusted single-qubit control, and use it to classify Lindbladian components. For the generically gauge dependent components, we construct Lindbladians to show that they can have $Ω(1)$ uncertainty independent of system size, even after imposing complete positivity.   We complement this characterization with SPAM-robust algorithms for learning every universally gauge-invariant component. Our algorithms use only trusted single-qubit operations, require neither ancillas nor entangling control, and use $\widetilde{\mathcal O}\left(ε^{-2}\log(N/δ)\right)$ experiments and total evolution time for constant locality and degree. Our guarantees allow global SPAM to become arbitrarily far from ideal as $N$ grows, requiring only nonvanishing local visibility. We also establish sufficient conditions for boundary-induced gauge invariance of additional Hamiltonian coefficients under physical positivity constraints, though learning these additional parameters in general remains an open problem. More broadly, our gauge-aware framework and SPAM-cancellation techniques offer a practical toolkit for the scalable characterization of open quantum systems.
summary: This paper tackles the difficult problem of extracting the true dynamics (Lindbladian) of an open quantum system from noisy measurements corrupted by SPAM noise. It mathematically proves that only certain 'gauge-invariant' parts of the dynamics are fundamentally measurable. The authors then develop efficient, resource-bounded quantum algorithms to estimate these robustly measurable parameters using only single-qubit operations.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental challenge of learning the parameters of a local Lindbladian describing open quantum system dynamics when the process is corrupted by State-Preparation-and-Measurement (SPAM) noise.
main_result: It provides a sharp characterization showing that only universally gauge-invariant components of the Lindbladian are fundamentally learnable, while others suffer from an irreducible uncertainty floor due to SPAM noise.
method: The authors employ gauge transformation theory to classify Lindbladian components and develop specialized, SPAM-robust quantum estimation algorithms restricted to single-qubit operations.
model_or_system: The system is an open quantum system whose dynamics are governed by a local Lindbladian $\mathcal{L}$, which is characterized by Hamiltonian coefficients and dissipative Kossakowski matrix elements. The learning is performed experimentally using only trusted single-qubit control.
key_observables: Lindbladian coefficients (Hamiltonian $h_c$ and dissipative $\alpha_{ab}$), and the ability to distinguish between universally gauge-invariant and generically gauge-dependent components.
important_parameters: The required experimental resources scale as $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(\epsilon^{-2}\log(N/\delta))$ for learnable components, where $\epsilon$ is the desired precision and $N$ is the system size.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of trusted single-qubit control and models the noise as SPAM noise, leading to the classification of learnable vs. unlearnable parameters.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the theoretical obstruction caused by SPAM noise, then using gauge theory to classify Lindbladian components into invariant and dependent sets, and finally constructing efficient, resource-bounded algorithms for the invariant components.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, resource-aware framework for characterizing open quantum systems from noisy experimental data, directly impacting the feasibility of quantum process tomography and quantum control.
